            A major version because something was removed: the Process section, /api/v1/processes and their database tables are gone. Runbooks are now Plugin Studio apps — a question that waits for a person, HTTP / TCP / console / inventory checks, diagnostics collection, the procedure's own text on every step and Simulate in the editor. On upgrade every process and run is written to data/process-backup-<stamp>.json before its table is dropped. Also in this release: API tokens granted per app, /api/v1/apps and read-only capabilities; Fortinet factory limits in Capacity Limits; Mass Deploy of approved templates; Installed software with OS and Python upgrades that always keep a rollback; a sidebar you can trim, a regrouped Settings menu, Security and Change Password in the Profile, and every table fitting its screen.

            Added

            • Runbooks as Plugin Studio apps. New app steps: Ask a person (the run waits and is answered on the run page, Yes / No or one button for a task), Load an appliance, HTTP check, TCP check, Console read, Appliance fact, Collect diagnostics and Activity; every step carries Instructions, Responsible and Estimated time. A check that could not look takes the error arrow, never no. The app editor has Simulate: the whole draft as a rehearsal, questions answered in place or Yes to every question, the path coloured on the diagram. App forms can list every appliance (Appliances (every product)).

            • Capacity Limits: one default limit for every row. A Default limit card on Administrator → Capacity Limits takes one percent of the Fortinet limit per product (for example 80). Every row without a number or percent of its own uses it, including rows that appear later (a new device, firmware or planned model), and Effective shows the resulting number on each row; automations and device health enforce it like any other limit. A row with its own value keeps it; Apply to all rows clears those values (overrides of the Fortinet number stay). The card also shows where monitoring warns, since the Thresholds warning is a percent of the effective limit (80 % of an 80 % limit = 64 % of Fortinet's). Audited as capacity.default_set / capacity.default_apply. Requested by the operator (translated from Spanish): "it needs to be more general too, add an extra filter like 80% that automatically puts the number on everything, so it's easier".

            • Plugin Studio: the FortiWeb pick honours the form. Pick a FortiWeb by capacity takes Objects the device must have (requires): certificate, server_pool, interface, web_protection_profile (a template id or a name). A FortiWeb with room that lacks one is skipped — read on the device when it answers, else the local cache — so a diagram no longer picks a FortiWeb by capacity alone and then fails on it at the certificate or the policy. Capacity is checked first (a database count); an empty value does not constrain; an unknown key is an error. When nothing qualifies, the error names, per FortiWeb, the limit or the missing object. Requested by the operator (translated from Spanish): "the FortiWeb must be chosen automatically from the variables entered, whether it is internal, and the capacities".

            • GET /api/v1/apps says how to fill each field: help, default (never a password field's), the options a select accepts and the console list a satom_select draws from (source). A caller had only the name, label and type.
            • API tokens: grants per Plugin Studio app. A token can now be handed exactly "run THIS app" — Access → Tokens → Apps it may run, one box per app. A grant is bound to the version an administrator approved (the published fields, diagram and actions). Change what the app runs and the grant pauses (403 grant_paused) until an administrator clicks Re-approve on the token, audited with both fingerprints; ticking the box again does not re-approve it. Deleting the app removes its grants from every token, audited per token, and a grant never follows a reused id to a different app. An empty list grants none. Requested by the operator (translated from Spanish): "is there a way to add processes and apps in SATOM and have them create a capability?".

            • /api/v1/apps: run a Plugin Studio app from outside. GET /apps lists the apps the token's owner may use in its ADOM (the console's access list and ADOM rules), with their form fields and whether the token may run them; POST /apps/<slug>/run runs the published version of a granted app in the background (202, poll GET /app-runs/<id>). A run from the API is unarmed by default — store writes, writing SQL, non-GET API calls and device changes are recorded as rehearsal: not executed, reads run for real — and "armed": true needs the new explicit capability app_arm. Migration tokgr01 adds api_tokens.process_grants and api_tokens.studio_app_grants.

            • API tokens: read capabilities metrics, findings and config_history. A token can now be handed exactly "read the metrics" and nothing else: metrics covers GET /metrics/query and the SATOM node readings (/system/nodes, /system/nodes/history), findings covers GET /findings, and config_history covers the configuration history and diffs. Until now metrics and findings answered to monitoring, the capability that also runs sweeps and scrapes. A token with no capability ticked reads all three, as before, and monitoring still implies metrics and findings, so no token issued earlier loses access. Requested by the operator (translated from Spanish): "SATOM has, for example, metrics that could be delivered via the API".

            • Capacity Limits show Fortinet's factory limits. Every limit used to be an empty field the admin had to fill in from the datasheet, so on a fresh install no automation ever had a ceiling to respect. The knowledge / API packs now carry Fortinet's published maximums (capacity-limits items of the docs section, from the Max Value Table API and Appendix B of the FortiWeb admin guide) per exact build, per CLI table and per hardware model, and SATOM stores them in capacity_factory. The page shows, per object type: In use · Fortinet limit (with the build and the source it came from) · Your limit — a number or a percent of the Fortinet limit · Effective (the lowest). The old Hard max field is now an Override, only for a box where Fortinet's number is wrong.
            • FortiWeb-VM limits are rules on the VM's memory, Fortinet's own: server policies = 20 for the first GB of RAM + 15 per extra GB, at most 256 (1024 from 64 GB); ADOMs and server pools by memory tier. SATOM evaluates them on the MemTotal of the last hardware scan, rounded down to whole GB as Fortinet specifies. The hourly device sync now rescans a FortiWeb's hardware when the last scan is missing or older than a week (read-only SSH); a VM never scanned shows "run a hardware scan" and blocks nothing.
            • A build with no document of its own uses the nearest build of the same major (shown as nearest build), never another major.
            • A device whose firmware field is empty (registered while its REST API was licence-locked) takes its build from the model string ("FortiWeb-KVM 8.0.6").
            • A factory limit the device already EXCEEDS is shown and NOT enforced: the box proves it accepts more, and blocking on a number it contradicts would stop work it would take. Your own limit still applies.
            • Cells where Fortinet's two sources disagree are flagged. On 8.0.6 the admin guide still carries git merge-conflict markers in five cells (>>>>>>> ddd581b1…) and disagrees with the API in eight; the API wins.
            • Four object types join the catalog: offline Web Protection Profiles (separate from inline — Fortinet publishes 256 of each per ADOM), server pools, virtual servers and virtual IPs. Each type is counted in the scope Fortinet counts it: per appliance (server policies, pools, VIPs — the whole chassis) or per ADOM (profiles, certificates, SNI, virtual servers).

            • The catalog is keyed by platform (FortiWeb-VM, FortiWeb-1000F), not by the string get system status prints: "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8" carried the firmware, so every patch release made a new "model" Fortinet publishes nothing for. Migration capfac01 re-keys existing rows (the row you filled in wins over empty duplicates). Every registered FortiWeb appears on the page on its own; Add model is for planning one you do not have. Requested by the operator: "they should be loaded with the harvester and in the updates, so the page shows the factory values and the user can enter a number or a percentage".

            • Operations › Automation › Mass Deploy. The newest approved version of every template of the ADOM, pushed to one or many of its devices in one canary-gated job: an SMTP server change, an NTP or DNS change, a Web Protection Profile for some devices only. It shows the targets with their build, fit and binding (a device bound to another version cannot be selected), a preview, then the deploy, plus a per-ADOM history with the result per device. It uses the Template Library's apply engine. FortiWeb ADOM; disabled with the reason in the other device ADOMs. Requested by the operator: "in Operations, Automation, Mass Deploy: the approved templates, to implement on one or several FortiWebs, for example a change in the SMTP, instead of going to each one; it must be per ADOM", and "WPP goes in too, because special ones can be created that are deployed only to some; they should not be put on all".

            • Secrets are typed at deploy time. A template never sends its own secret values (passwords, PSKs, private keys). Each one is left out of the push, so the device keeps its own, unless a value is typed in Mass Deploy. A typed value is not stored, logged or echoed: the job record, the change history and the preview show <secret>.

            • Approving a Web Protection Profile template asks which devices it governs: every FortiWeb of the ADOM (deployed now, as before) or only the devices picked in Mass Deploy (nothing deployed or locked until a device is bound). Mass Deploy binds the devices of such a template, and can limit a fleet-wide one to the selected devices.

            • Settings › Appearance › Sidebar menu: hide entries, submenus and groups. A tree of everything the sidebar draws in every ADOM; an unticked row leaves the sidebar of every user in every ADOM it appears in (Architecture is one row, not one per ADOM), live and disabled alike, and a group or submenu left empty goes with it. Hiding is not a permission: the page still opens by link and still needs its own permission. Settings, the ADOM switcher and the device picker cannot be hidden; a device's own menu only as a whole. Requested by the operator: "in Settings, Appearance, add the option to remove menu and submenu entries, for example the Architecture menu when it is not needed".

            • Plugin Studio › Apps: certificates already on the FortiWebs. A new SATOM list, FortiWeb local certificates, offers the local certificates of every FortiWeb from the local cache, each naming the FortiWebs that hold it. The Certificate step has a third mode, device: it uses a certificate that is already on the appliance, checks the name on the device before anything is written (a missing one stops the run), and writes nothing itself. A certificate the Certificate Manager also knows keeps its provider's zone rule. Requested by the operator: "the plugin cannot show the certificates we have; it should show the ones on the FortiWebs".

            • Plugin Studio › Apps: searchable lists. Any list field (fixed, data store, API or SATOM list) can be marked searchable in the Form tab. It then gets a search box where every word must match, with a matches / total counter. A choice the user made stays selected while they search, and Enter in the box never runs the app. Requested by the operator: "some fields should have a search when the user wants one".

            • Settings › General › Installed software: every package this installation runs on and its installed version, per node. Platform components (Python, PostgreSQL server and client, nginx, VictoriaMetrics, Redis, OpenSSL, CA certificates, OpenSSH, Git, rsync, curl, sudo, bubblewrap, Lua, systemd, kernel) show the version the program reports and the distribution package version (dpkg/rpm) that security advisories name. Python packages lists the whole interpreter, with requirements.txt entries marked direct. Browser assets come from the vendor manifest. Versions that are not the same on every node are marked differs, and a silent peer shows as unreachable. Read-only and admin-only, with a JSON download. Requested by the operator: "a section with all the packages the system uses and the installed version, for example nginx".

            • Installed software: check for and apply OS updates for every component except the kernel (it belongs to the host). Check for updates refreshes each node's package index and lists what is newer; Upgrade runs the node's own package manager on the installed packages only (apt-get install --only-upgrade keeping local config, dnf upgrade, yum update, zypper update; Arch is refused, it does not support partial upgrades). From the primary, "all nodes" upgrades the standby first and this node only after it succeeded. Restarts follow the component (SATOM for Python and its OpenSSL, nginx after nginx -t, health checks after PostgreSQL and Redis), nothing restarts when nothing changed, and services still on a replaced library are reported. VictoriaMetrics goes to the version the signed release pins, never "latest". Requested by the operator: "can those packages also be upgraded? Leave only the kernel out; remember the command depends on the OS".
            • Rollback for every upgrade, from the web and from the console. Before an OS package upgrade, SATOM simulates the transaction and saves every package it replaces (dependencies included) at its current version, from the repositories or rebuilt with dpkg-repack; before a Python change it saves a full copy of the venv. No copy, no change. A failed upgrade or health check puts the copy back by itself. Installed software › Rollback points restores any saved point, and satom execute rollback list / satom execute rollback apply <id> --yes do the same from the console with the web, the database, the network and the venv down (they run the signed root-owned runner with the system Python). Ten OS and three Python points are kept per node in /var/lib/satom-rollback.
            • Upgrade any Python package from Installed software. Check for updates also lists newer versions of every package in the venv (against the index of Update sources; an unusable index is reported, never replaced by pypi.org), and each can be upgraded on its own, protected by the venv copy. Only installed packages; direct requirements keep their pin in sync, transitive ones are not pinned. Libraries changes now roll back from the venv copy too instead of reinstalling the old version from the index. Requested by the operator: "Python packages should also be upgradable; what matters is that a rollback is possible, even from the console, so that if something fails it can always be repaired".

            Changed

            • Menu: Change Management Types and Triggers moved (operator request). Change Types is now Change Mgt Types (page title Change Management Types), an entry of Administrator → Objects instead of the Change Management section. Triggers left Administrator for Automation → Automations, where it is a third tab next to Scheduled and On a trigger (administrators only; the address /administration/triggers/ is unchanged).

            • Every table fits the screen; row actions stay on one line. Measured on the 690 pages of every ADOM menu and their detail pages at 1280, 1366, 1600 and 1920 px wide. A table wider than its box now first lets headers and text wrap between words (names, badges, numbers, dates and actions stay on one line), shows a very long value (a certificate, an image, a message body) on one line with an ellipsis and the full value on hover, and only then hides its least useful columns behind "N columns hidden · Show all". Tables of the measured device GUI pages use the full width too. Rows with many actions keep the main ones visible and move the rest into a "…" menu (Appliances, Plugin Studio, Deep monitors, Service Monitor, Report Studio, API Tokens). Toolbars that wrapped are on one line (device GUI lists, Lua editor, Transaction Tracer, appliance page, Thresholds scope, API explorers), buttons in one row have one size, and buttons keep at least 8 px from the text next to them. Plugin Studio's Explorer becomes a strip of tabs above the content below 1400 px. Requested by the operator: "the table may not appear complete depending on the resolution … it can always use 100% of the screen, but it has to fit; the actions or buttons must be in line and not on multiple lines, it doesn't look professional".

            • Sidebar: menus and submenus share one size and typeface; the current page and its path stay highlighted. First-level heads (Operations, Administrator, Device, Plugin Studio) were 10px uppercase while every entry below them is 13.5px; they now use the same 13.5px type, 14px icon and 37px row, told apart by weight. The current page had the sidebar's own blue as its background, so only the thin amber rail marked it: it now gets a white wash and a bold label, and every menu and submenu that holds it keeps a bold label and an amber icon, folded or not. A label too long for the rail now ends in an ellipsis instead of being cut mid-letter at the edge, and the favourites star no longer takes room from the label it sits on. Settings gets the same treatment: its group heads (System, Integrations, AI...) were 11px capitals over 13px entries and now share their size, and the group and sub-menu holding the open pane stay marked. Requested by the operator: "check the size of the menus and submenus, make sure they are the same size and typeface, and keep the active menu or submenu highlighted so it is easier to see".

            • The console now ships its typeface: Inter 4.1. The stylesheets asked for Inter but no copy of it shipped, so every browser drew its own system font (Segoe UI on Windows, San Francisco on macOS, DejaVu on Linux) and the console looked and measured different on every workstation. The variable Inter (roman and italic, app/static/vendor/inter/, SIL Open Font License 1.1, byte-identical to the upstream release) is now served locally like every other vendored asset, so offline installs get it too.

            • Device Provisioning and System Provisioning moved to Administrator › Devices, in every ADOM, with the same rules as before: System Provisioning is live in FortiWeb, greyed out with the reason in the other device ADOMs and not drawn in Global. Device Provisioning is drawn only while a hypervisor is registered (an enabled row in Settings › Hypervisors), whatever Settings › Appearance › Sidebar menu says; without one the page could only offer Config only, and existing machines are added in Appliances and configured in System Provisioning. The page still opens by URL. A profile without user management has no Administrator group and still finds both in Automation, as with Device Console. No permission changed. Requested by the operator: "System Provisioning and Device Provisioning should be in Administrator", and that it should not show without a hypervisor integration.

            • Scout leaves the sidebar until it is configured. The Scout entry (Operations › Troubleshooting, every ADOM) is drawn only when Scout is switched on in Settings › Scout ▸ Providers AND at least one provider can take a message (not disabled; inside the LAN unless external providers are allowed). Otherwise it is not drawn at all, even when Settings › Appearance › Sidebar menu has it ticked; the page still opens by URL. Settings › Scout now seeds the disabled local Ollama provider, which only the Scout page did before. The WAF exception advice uses the same test, so a switched-on Scout whose only provider is disabled no longer counts as available. Requested by the operator: "if Scout is not configured it should not appear in the menu, even if it is active in Settings › Appearance".

            • Sentinel follows the same rule: not configured, not in the menu. Monitoring › Sentinel (Global ADOM) is offered only while Sentinel is configured: switched on AND at least one FortiWeb you can see that is not retired (host *.invalid), because the FortiWeb attack log is all its sweep ingests; a FortiWeb in maintenance still counts. Path Diagnostics does not follow Scout's gate: it does not use Scout's AI (the ladder is deterministic), so it stays in the menu while Scout is unconfigured, and switched off it is still drawn disabled with the reason. Requested by the operator: "if Scout is not configured, the things related to it must disappear from the menu, and the same for Sentinel", then "if it is not included in Scout, show it".

            • Monitoring › Device health: devices grouped by ADOM, problems on the card. The cards are now grouped in one collapsible section per ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate); a section's title takes the colour of its worst device and shows how many are critical, in warning or unknown. The rows of errors at the top of the page are gone: a device with a problem is shown by the colour of its own card, and a click on the card opens what is wrong and how to fix it — concrete steps per signal (harvest, cache, deep monitors, capacity), built from the same reading the badge comes from. A section you fold or open stays that way; untouched, a section opens when it holds a problem. The page now uses the console's light badge colours throughout.

            • Deep monitors, Service Monitor and Analytics explain how they differ. Each page has a Which page? button in its header that opens the same comparison: the question each page answers, how it measures, and when to use it, with the page you are on marked and links to the other two.
            • Monitoring › Sentinel: clearer health cards. The four cards (Pipeline, Behavioural baseline, CVE mirror, Response engine) carry their state as a coloured edge, an icon and a badge, the heartbeat age reads in s/min/h, and the baseline shows a meter. (When the Monitoring › Sentinel entry is offered: see Changed above.)
            • Wiki: Follow and Confluence move onto the articles. Each article's card in the list now has its own Follow button (as the article page does), and ADOMs, Global and everything are followed from one Follow button above the article list that unfolds one box per ADOM; the Following link left the Wiki menu (the full list, with the e-mail choice, is linked from that button). The Groups link left the Wiki menu too (groups stay in Administrator › Access › Groups). Confluence connections moved to Settings › Integrations › Confluence (administrators) and no longer fix a space or parent page: the new Confluence button on each card and on the article page opens a dialog where the publisher picks the space from the ones the connection sees and, once a space is picked, the parent page from its page tree or by searching its titles. An article can now have a page in several spaces; publishing again to a space updates its page where it is. Old Wiki › Confluence links land on the new card. Requested by the operator: "Following should be above where the articles start, just a button that unfolds to pick which ADOM; a follow button on each article's card and inside the article; remove the Groups button; the Confluence integration belongs in Settings › Integrations, with a button like the subscription one on the card and in the article so that article is the one that goes to Confluence; the user only picks the space, and the parent appears once the space is picked, with a search and the tree".
            • Calendar: System Automations are off by default, and the bands are checkboxes saved to your profile. Show is now a row of checkboxes — Planned changes, Automations, System Automations, What already ran — and every tick is saved on your profile at once (the Remember for me step is gone; Reset to default goes back to the default view). System Automations start unticked. An unticked band says what it is holding back next to its box, for example (14 hidden · 230 runs), instead of the old "N of M drawn" banners. The last band that carries the grid stays ticked and locked. Requested by the operator: "remove all the system automations by default, only enabled through a checkbox; make the other filters checkboxes too and save in the profile what the user wants".

            • Calendar: Plan a change opens in a modal from a Plan a change button at the top right of the page, instead of a card under the day panel. The form and the process are the same, and its window still follows the day you pick. Requested by the operator.

            • Settings menu regrouped, one level deeper. System › General is now a sub-menu holding General, Node TLS, Email & Alerts and Thresholds; Integrations is a group of its own (Integrations, DNS Records, Hypervisors); AI holds Scout (Providers, Path Diagnostics, Architecture) and Sentinel (its six entries, unchanged). The Network & DNS, Monitoring & Alerts, Sentinel and Path Diagnostics groups are gone: 8 groups, 37 panels. Pane targets (#tab-…) did not change. Requested by the operator.

            • Every Settings card has a title, starts folded and has its own anchor (/settings/#card-…, the same in every language). A link to a card switches to its panel, opens it and folds the others; a panel with one card draws it open, and the card you saved is open again after the redirect. Status tiles are never folded.
            • DNS Lookup's resolver list moved to Administrator › Objects › DNS Resolvers (/dns-lookup/resolvers, admin-only): the list of DNS servers the lookup asks is a page of its own, in every ADOM, and the DNS Lookup page links to it from its DNS servers panel. DNS Lookup itself is also offered under Administrator › System. Old /settings/#tab-dnstool and /dns-lookup/#resolvers links forward to the new page, and saving the list returns there.
            • Security and Change Password moved from Settings to your Profile. The two-factor authentication, recovery email, active session and password cards are now at the top of Profile (user menu, top right); Settings no longer has a My Account group, so every Settings group is admin-only. A non-admin who opens /settings/ is sent to the Profile, the sidebar offers Settings only to administrators, and old links to #tab-security / #tab-password land on the same cards. The form URLs are unchanged. Requested by the operator: "put My Account in the profile so it is not in Settings".

            Fixed

            • Tables without a frame, text against the edge (operator request: some tables had no border and the first column's text touched the table edge). Every data table now leaves 14 px before the first column and after the last, and a table that floats inside a card body (the dashboard's Fleet list, Sentinel, System Backup, Settings, Registry…) gets a rounded outline. Measured on the 102 console pages that render a table: 171 tables, none under 12 px except the calendar grid; only a table nested in another table stays without a frame.
            • Lua Studio: Delete did nothing. Its form was nested inside the editor form, so the browser dropped it; it is now its own form.
            • Capacity counted every object twice. The device cache keeps an object in both its config and deep layers, and the count added both: {device} showed 100 server policies against the 50 show server-policy policy lists over SSH, so the guardrails and the health grade read twice the real usage. Objects are now counted once per (type, key).

            • UI strings rendered in English in every other language. 91 strings (Mass Deploy, the Confluence connection, the monitoring help, the calendar filter notice and this round's capacity labels) had no Spanish, German, French or Italian translation; the catalogue-coverage guard was red on main. All are translated.

            • A capability-restricted API token could read every recorded configuration of its ADOM. GET /appliances/<id>/config-history and config-diff checked the scope and the ADOM but no capability, so a token restricted to, say, backend_edit read the whole configuration history. Such a token now needs config_history (403 capability_denied otherwise), and the check answers before the device lookup, so a restricted token cannot probe which device ids exist. A token with no capability ticked is unchanged.

            • Sidebar: a long Plugin Studio app name is readable and can be starred. An app is named by its author (up to 120 characters), and on one line "New FortiWeb server policy (DDI + certificate)" showed about half its name, with the favourite star drawn over the last letters. App entries stay on one line and end in an ellipsis that stops short of the star, and the link tooltip carries the whole name.

            • The change history stored write payloads in clear, including any password a write carried, and the device's ENC ciphertext in the before-snapshot. Both are masked now, and so is the result kept in a fleet-apply job's record.

            • A fleet rollout from the Template Library ignored device bindings: applying to several devices pushed the chosen version even to a device pinned to another one. It is refused now, with the reason.

            • Apply to a device SATOM cannot push templates to (anything but FortiWeb) is refused in the preview instead of being sent through the FortiWeb writer.

            • Jobs: the table fits the screen at every resolution. It needed 1470 px and scrolled sideways below a ~1830 px window. The job ID now sits under the job type, duration under the start time, long owners and messages wrap (messages clamp to two lines); below 1400 px Owner and Where fold into the job cell as chips, below 1200 px Started does too and Pause/Resume/Stop become icon buttons. Status badges use the light-theme colours (yellow/green on white were barely legible). Reported by the operator: "the jobs table does not fit the screen at some resolutions".

            • Deep monitors / Service Monitor: closing a chart left the screen dimmed. Every visit to the page added another copy of its click handlers, so from the second visit one click opened the chart (and the history, policy, edit and discover dialogs) several times; closing removed one backdrop and left the rest. The handlers are now dropped when you leave the page, each dialog reuses one instance, and the console removes any backdrop left behind once the last dialog closes. The same click doubling also made a device card fold and unfold in one click.

            • Certificate Manager › certificates on the devices no longer shows a FortiWeb that refuses the REST call (HTTP 423, -20010: the license of the HA peer is not valid) as online with 0 certificates. The box is now marked unreachable, with the device's own message.

            Removed

            • The Process section is gone (operator request: "this belongs in Plugin Studio, as an app that does the whole process"). Administrator → Process, its diagrams and runs, /api/v1/processes, the Walk a process scheduled action, automation kind and app step, XML import/export and the process_arm token capability were removed; the database tables are dropped on upgrade after every process and run is written to data/process-backup-<date>.json. Runbooks are Plugin Studio apps (see Added). The Change Management section of Administrator went with it.
